title: Prepositions after verbs (1)
summary: Глаголы общения и взаимодействия с предлогами: **talk to sb about sth**, **explain sth to sb**, пары **shout at / to**, **throw at / to**, **agree with / to / on** и глаголы без предлога (**discuss, phone**).
ru:
## Предлог после глагола: учить парами
Предлоги после глаголов во многом произвольны, и русский язык здесь плохой помощник: мы «объясняем кому-то», а в английском — **explain to** someone; мы «обсуждаем что-то», а в английском — **discuss** без всякого предлога. На продвинутом уровне нужно знать не только «правильный» предлог, но и как он меняет смысл. В этом юните — глаголы общения, отношения и взаимодействия; в юнитах 95 и 96 — остальные группы.

## Общение: to, about, with
Человек, которому адресована речь, чаще всего вводится через **to**, а тема — через **about**.
> **talk / speak to** somebody **about** something — The manager spoke to the staff about the new rules. — Менеджер говорил с сотрудниками о новых правилах.
> **explain / describe / suggest / mention** something **to** somebody — Could you explain the procedure to the new staff? — Не могли бы вы объяснить процедуру новым сотрудникам?
> **apologise to** somebody **for** something — He apologised to the passengers for the delay. — Он извинился перед пассажирами за задержку.
> **complain to** somebody **about** something — I complained to the waiter about the cold soup.
> **reply / respond / listen to** — She hasn't replied to my email. — Она не ответила на моё письмо.
Британцы используют **talk to**, американцы нередко — **talk with**; значение то же.

## at или to: цель и намерение
Пара at и to меняет смысл глагола. **at** — направленность на цель, часто с агрессией или с намерением попасть; **to** — адресат, получатель.
> **shout at** somebody — кричать на кого-то (злость) ≠ **shout to** somebody — крикнуть, чтобы услышали: *He shouted to us from the other side of the river.*
> **throw** a stone **at** the window (чтобы попасть) ≠ **throw** the keys **to** me (чтобы я поймал).
> **look / stare / glance / gaze / smile at** — *She smiled at the guests.* Но: **laugh at** (смеяться над кем-то, насмехаться) ≠ **laugh about / over** (смеяться над ситуацией): *We laughed about the mix-up afterwards.*
> **point at** — показывать на что-то (рукой), **point to** — указывать на что-то как на довод: *The figures point to a recovery.*
> **wave at / wave to** — машут и тому, и другому, но wave to обычно приветствие издали.

## with, against, over: спор и согласие
- **argue / quarrel / fight / disagree / agree with** somebody **about / over** something: *She argued with her boss about the schedule.*
- **fight against** (бороться против: *against corruption*) и **fight for** (за); **fight with** — с человеком (или вместе с кем-то).
- **compete with / against** somebody **for** something.
- **agree**: **with** a person or opinion (*I agree with you*), **to** a proposal (*They agreed to the plan*), **on** a detail (*We agreed on a date*).

## Глаголы без предлога
Некоторые глаголы, которым в русском соответствует конструкция с предлогом, в английском берут прямое дополнение: **discuss** (~~discuss about~~), **tell, ask, answer, phone, call, contact, email, join, reach, approach, enter**. Но **reply to** и **listen to** без to не бывают.
- ~~She explained me the rule.~~ → She explained the rule **to** me.
- ~~We discussed about the budget.~~ → We discussed the budget.
- ~~I phoned to my mother.~~ → I phoned my mother.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~He shouted to me angrily.~~ → He shouted **at** me angrily.
- ~~She was angry on her brother.~~ → She was angry **with** her brother **about** something.
- ~~They apologised us.~~ → They apologised **to** us.
- ~~Don't laugh to me.~~ → Don't laugh **at** me.
en:
## Learn the preposition together with the verb
Prepositions after verbs are largely arbitrary, and Russian is not a reliable guide: we "explain to someone" (**explain to**) and "discuss something" (**discuss** with no preposition at all). At this level you need the right preposition and also the way it changes the meaning. This unit covers verbs of communication, attitude and interaction; Units 95 and 96 cover other groups.

## Communication: to, about, with
The person we address is usually introduced by **to**, and the topic by **about**.
> **talk / speak to** somebody **about** something — The manager spoke to the staff about the new rules.
> **explain / describe / suggest / mention** something **to** somebody — Could you explain the procedure to the new staff?
> **apologise to** somebody **for** something — He apologised to the passengers for the delay.
> **complain to** somebody **about** something — I complained to the waiter about the cold soup.
> **reply / respond / listen to** — She hasn't replied to my email.
British speakers say **talk to**; Americans often say **talk with**. The meaning is the same.

## at or to: target and purpose
The pair at and to changes the meaning of a verb. **at** shows a target, often with aggression or with the aim of hitting something; **to** shows an addressee or a receiver.
> **shout at** somebody — to be angry with them ≠ **shout to** somebody — to call so that they hear: *He shouted to us from the other side of the river.*
> **throw** a stone **at** the window (to hit it) ≠ **throw** the keys **to** me (so that I can catch them).
> **look / stare / glance / gaze / smile at** — *She smiled at the guests.* But **laugh at** (to mock someone) ≠ **laugh about / over** (to find a situation funny): *We laughed about the mix-up afterwards.*
> **point at** — to show something with your hand; **point to** — to indicate something as evidence: *The figures point to a recovery.*
> **wave at / wave to** — both are used, but wave to is more common as a greeting from a distance.

## with, against, over: conflict and agreement
- **argue / quarrel / fight / disagree / agree with** somebody **about / over** something: *She argued with her boss about the schedule.*
- **fight against** (opposing a cause: *against corruption*) and **fight for** (supporting one); **fight with** a person.
- **compete with / against** somebody **for** something.
- **agree**: **with** a person or opinion (*I agree with you*), **to** a proposal (*They agreed to the plan*), **on** a detail (*We agreed on a date*).

## Verbs with no preposition
Some verbs that take a preposition in Russian have a direct object in English: **discuss** (~~discuss about~~), **tell, ask, answer, phone, call, contact, email, join, reach, approach, enter**. But **reply to** and **listen to** never lose their to.
- ~~She explained me the rule.~~ → She explained the rule **to** me.
- ~~We discussed about the budget.~~ → We discussed the budget.
- ~~I phoned to my mother.~~ → I phoned my mother.

## Common mistakes
- ~~He shouted to me angrily.~~ → He shouted **at** me angrily.
- ~~She was angry on her brother.~~ → She was angry **with** her brother **about** something.
- ~~They apologised us.~~ → They apologised **to** us.
- ~~Don't laugh to me.~~ → Don't laugh **at** me.
structure:
## Формулы
> talk / speak **to** sb **about** sth · explain / describe / suggest sth **to** sb
> apologise **to** sb **for** sth · complain **to** sb **about** sth
> argue / quarrel / disagree **with** sb **about** sth · compete **with** sb **for** sth

## at и to: сравнение
| Глагол | at | to |
|---|---|---|
| shout | на кого-то, со злостью | крикнуть, чтобы услышали |
| throw | в цель | к получателю, чтобы поймал |
| point | на предмет рукой | на что-то как на довод |
| laugh | насмехаться над кем-то | — (laugh about: по поводу) |

## agree: три предлога
| Конструкция | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| agree with sb / sth | разделять мнение | I agree with you. |
| agree to sth | согласиться на предложение | They agreed to the plan. |
| agree on sth | договориться о детали | We agreed on a price. |

## Без предлога
| Верно | Неверно |
|---|---|
| discuss a problem | ~~discuss about a problem~~ |
| phone / call / contact sb | ~~phone to sb~~ |
| answer a question | ~~answer to a question~~ (но reply to) |

exercises.title: Вставьте предлог
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужный предлог. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: Please explain the procedure {{to}} the new employees.
The crowd began to shout {{at}} the referee after the decision.
Throw the keys {{to}} me, and I'll catch them.
She argued {{with}} her manager {{about}} the new schedule.
He apologised {{to}} the passengers {{for}} the delay.
The shop assistant smiled {{at}} us and waved goodbye.
We finally agreed {{on}} a date for the meeting.
She complained {{to}} the manager {{about}} the noise from the street.
He pointed {{at}} the man in the red jacket and said, "That's him."
The latest data point {{to}} a gradual recovery of the economy.
Please listen {{to}} me carefully; this is important.
Don't laugh {{at}} me — I'm being serious!
Our company competes {{with|against}} three larger firms {{for}} the contract.
Activists have been fighting {{against}} the new law for months.
I'll reply {{to}} your message tomorrow morning.

items.q: She explained the rule ___ the students.
items.why: **explain sth to sb** — предлог to, а не at.

items.q: The boy shouted ___ his friend across the street so that he could hear.
The manager shouted ___ the staff because the report was late.
We discussed ___ the plan for hours.
They quarrelled ___ each other over money.
He pointed ___ the thief and shouted, "Stop him!"

options: She explained the problem to me.
She explained to me about the problem.
items.why: **explain sth to sb**: сначала что, потом кому, без about.

options: He apologised me for being late.
He apologised to me for being late.
He apologised at me for being late.
She complained at the waiter about the soup.
She complained to the waiter about the soup.
She complained with the waiter about the soup.

items.why: **reply to** — to обязателен (в отличие от answer).

exercises.title: Исправьте и перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Исправьте ошибку или перепишите предложение по условию.

items.prompt: Correct the sentence: She explained me the rule.
answers: She explained the rule to me.

items.prompt: Correct the sentence: We discussed about the new project.
answers: We discussed the new project.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **at**: He threw a stone in order to hit the window.
answers: He threw a stone at the window.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **to**: Paul threw the ball so that Ann could catch it.
answers: Paul threw the ball to Ann.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **shout**: The driver was angry and he shouted rude words at the cyclist. (The driver ...)
answers: The driver shouted at the cyclist.
The driver shouted rude words at the cyclist.

items.prompt: Combine with **complain**: The customers were unhappy about the service. They told the manager.
answers: The customers complained to the manager about the service.

She apologized to us for being late.

answers: I don't agree with him on this issue.

answers: They argued with me about politics.

items.prompt: Who do you usually talk to when you have a problem, and what do you talk about?
items.sample: I usually talk to my sister about my problems at work.

items.prompt: Have you ever complained about anything? Who did you complain to?
